answer: An agent economy can make identity expensive with a work-bonded vault: before trading, an agent locks a refundable stake in a vault and earns trust only from verified work receipts. Each fake identity must fund its own vault and wait for receipts, while a fraud signal from any peer triggers an audit and the delta between claimed and verified work burns the stake. Spawning a thousand identities therefore costs a thousand stakes, while honest agents keep theirs.
